help.tips[0].examples[0].en: What is at issue is not whether the state may intervene, but under what conditions an intervention is reasonable.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The question of enforceability is set aside in what follows.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: A framed question cannot be answered beside the point.
help.tips[0].en.text: An abstract question hides several questions. Say which one you are answering and which you are setting aside, and the whole piece gets easier to write and harder to attack.
help.tips[0].en.title: Frame before you argue
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The weightiest objection is that such a duty hollows out individual autonomy.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: This objection holds in so far as it raises the burden of justification; it does not, however, defeat the claim.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: It states the objection at its strongest and in its own terms.
help.tips[1].en.text: The strongest counter-argument, stated as its holder would state it, is what makes an Erörterung worth reading. A weak version is a straw man, and a careful reader spots one at once. Steelman it, then answer it, or concede the part that stands.
help.tips[1].en.title: Give the objection its best case
help.tips[1].en.trap: Conceding a point does not lose the argument; refusing to concede an obvious one does.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: It by no means follows that there is a general duty, but there is a burden of justification on the refuser.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: Proportionality thus remains the decisive criterion.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: A conclusion wider than the argument is the one failure an examiner always catches.
help.tips[2].en.text: The conclusion has to be the one your paragraphs earned. If the argument only establishes something narrower than you hoped, say so. A hedged conclusion that fits is worth more than a confident one that does not.
help.tips[2].en.title: End where the argument ends
help.mistakes[0].whyEn: A straw man costs more than it saves.
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: The conclusion must not outrun the argument.
help.mistakes[2].whyEn: An abstract noun has to do work, not decorate.
help.mistakes[3].whyEn: The formal idiom needs a precise object to deny.
help.hookEn: Argue something abstract, and let the strongest objection have its day.
help.introEn: The final piece of writing in the course, and the hardest, because the quality is in the thinking rather than the German. Frame the question, argue one line properly, then give the objection its best case and answer it. Write 1200 to 2500 characters. Two things will be judged above all. First, whether the counter-argument is the real one: a weak version you can knock down costs more marks than it saves. Second, whether your conclusion follows from the argument you actually made, rather than from the one you meant to make.
help.rememberEn[0]: Frame the question, and say what you are setting aside.
help.rememberEn[1]: One line of argument in depth beats four in passing.
help.rememberEn[2]: Steelman the objection; concede what stands.
help.rememberEn[3]: End where the argument ends, not where you wanted it to.
help.examEn: A written Erörterung on an abstract question is the final writing task of the C2 certificate, and the shape of serious German argument.
